from typing import TypedDict


class GarageDoorData(TypedDict):
    """Aladdin door data"""

    device_id: str
    door_number: int
    name: str
    status: str
    link_status: str
    battery_level: int


class GarageDoor:
    """Aladdin Garage Door Entity"""

    def __init__(self, data: GarageDoorData) -> None:
        self.device_id: str = data["device_id"]
        self.door_number: int = data["door_number"]
        self.unique_id: str = f"{self.device_id}-{self.door_number}"
        self.name: str = data["name"]
        self.status: str | None = data["status"]
        self.link_status: str | None = data["link_status"]
        self.battery_level: int | None = data["battery_level"]

Key points about the implementation:

- **`config_entry`** uses `async_redact_data(config_entry.data, TO_REDACT)` — this recurses into nested dicts, so it redacts `access_token`/`refresh_token` wherever they live (in this OAuth2 integration they sit under `data["token"]`). I used `CONF_ACCESS_TOKEN` (which resolves to `"access_token"`) plus the literal `"refresh_token"`.
- **`doors`** is built from `config_entry.runtime_data`, which is the `dict[unique_id, AladdinConnectCoordinator]` set up in `__init__.py`. Each door is keyed by its `unique_id` (already formatted as `{device_id}-{door_number}` by the SDK's `GarageDoor`) and exposes exactly the six required fields pulled from `coordinator.data`.
